claim: AAAI-27 authors must select exactly one mandatory primary keyword and up to five optional secondary topics from a list of 200+ topics organized under 17 top-level submission areas.
quoted_support: In AAAI-27 authors are asked to choose one primary keyword (mandatory) and (optionally) up to five secondary topics. With over 200 topics available to choose from, picking the best keywords for a paper may become confusing.

claim: There is no standalone 'ML: Calibration' keyword at AAAI-27; calibration and confidence-related work falls under 'ML: Bayesian Learning & Uncertainty Quantification', with 'ML: Evaluation, Benchmarking, Datasets & Analysis' and 'NLP: Interpretability, Analysis & Evaluation (incl. Factuality & Hallucination)' as adjacent candidates depending on framing.
stance_target: Correct primary-keyword selection for a code-LLM calibration paper at AAAI-27
scope_conditions: Verbatim AAAI-27 keyword list under ML and NLP areas
quoted_support: ML: Bayesian Learning & Uncertainty Quantification ... ML: Evaluation, Benchmarking, Datasets & Analysis ... NLP: Interpretability, Analysis & Evaluation (incl. Factuality & Hallucination)

claim: AAAI-27's official guidance states the primary topic should reflect where the paper's main methodological contribution lies: a general ML advance merely demonstrated on code/NLP applications should be filed under ML, not the application area, unless the contribution fundamentally exploits code- or language-specific structure.
stance_target: Rubric for choosing between ML vs. NLP vs. Software-Engineering primary keyword for a code-calibration paper
scope_conditions: AAAI-27 author guidance for intersectional papers
quoted_support: if an ML algorithm is demonstrated on both computer vision and NLP applications, it is best kept under ML (as it is a general advance, with NLP and vision serving only as applications). If, however, the paper is heavily motivated by details of a particular class of ML problems...then picking a topic that focuses on this class of problems...is more appropriate.
